page: Microsoft Azure E128-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for enterprise workloads that require high memory capacity relative to compute footprint. Powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The processor operates at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz, supported by 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 instructions.

The defining characteristic of this configuration is its high memory-to-core ratio, delivering 1024.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 32.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is fully bundled, providing 7559 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity. The instance lacks discrete GPU acceleration, relying entirely on the AMD EPYC processor for computational tasks.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread and core-level compute capabilities, achieving top-tier ratings in stress-ng single-core tests and Geekbench single-core scores of 2884.0. Multi-core execution is solid with a Geekbench multi-core score of 22126.0 and top-tier compression metrics, including 41.3 GB/sec in gzip. Because raw core count is limited to 32 vCPUs on a high-memory chassis, multi-threaded stress testing and large-model LLM generation yield average to low performance relative to compute-dense architectures, confirming that this shape trades massive parallel compute for dense memory allocation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance avoids the unnecessary licensing costs of higher vCPU counts while preserving a full 1 TB memory allocation and expansive local NVMe storage. This architecture is an effective fit for large-scale in-memory databases like Redis or SAP HANA, enterprise relational database management systems, heavy caching tiers, and memory-bound ETL analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E128-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores based on x86_64 architecture, clocked at 4.5 GHz with AVX-512 extensions. The server is configured with 1024.0 GB of RAM, establishing a high 32 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes 7559 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage without discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core execution with a Geekbench single-core score of 2884.0 and strong compression throughput, though multi-core throughput and unaccelerated large LLM inference remain modest due to the constrained core count. By pairing a massive memory footprint and fast NVMe disk with a restrained compute profile, the instance optimizes resource allocation for memory-constrained workloads without incurring superfluous vCPU costs. It is suited for in-memory databases, large caching layers, high-volume transactional databases, and memory-intensive analytics engines.
